The background crowd is blurred by shallow depth of field, leaving only shifting color patches and the edge of a newsstand as spatial cues. Side-backlighting outlines the contours of his cheeks and hat brim. Don't make me repeat myself!' shot3: The third shot enters with a quick hard cut into a side-lit close-up, bringing the camera closer to the tense atmosphere between the two characters. The composition uses a compressed front-and-back arrangement: in the foreground, the old man in the gray jacket slightly raises his finger but stops just short of personal space, while the focus rests on their flushed faces, trembling lips, and intense eye contact. Warm reflections from the street combined with side lighting accentuate skin texture and wrinkles. Meanwhile, the cane-wielding elder exhales heavily, initially avoiding eye contact before quickly locking gazes. The camera makes an extremely subtle lateral shift, emphasizing the psychological tug-of-war where neither party yields.
shot4: Shot 4 transitions from the previous shot via a brief hard cut, switching to overhead medium shot panning along the sidewalk edge. Brick patterns and curb form stable horizontal structure. Onlookers gradually stop in the background, forming a semi-circular encirclement but maintaining distance. Lighting remains warm natural light, with slight shadows on faces enhancing tension. Both men pull apart emotionally, one tapping cane to steady himself, the other spreading hands to emphasize stance—no shoving. Nearby, someone inhales sharply, others pause and look back. The camera pans along the sidewalk, conveying bystander pressure and increasing stillness in the air.
shot5: Shot 5 connects to the previous shot with a slightly slower fade-in/fade-out, transitioning into a medium close-up that slowly pulls back. The composition initially focuses on the chest of the elderly man with the cane, rising and falling with anger, and his tightly clenched hand gripping the cane. Then, the camera gradually pulls back to include the other elderly man within the same frame. The two stand facing each other, separated by half a step, neither moving closer.
